interactions.warning: Aspirin combined with Warfarin significantly increases bleeding risk. Avoid concurrent use unless a clinician explicitly supervises INR monitoring.
Ibuprofen can interfere with the cardioprotective effect of low-dose Aspirin and raise gastrointestinal bleeding risk.
Paracetamol with alcohol or above-max daily dose can cause severe liver injury. Keep total intake at or below 4g/day in adults and avoid alcohol.
Acetaminophen (Paracetamol) plus alcohol increases the risk of acute hepatic toxicity.
Amoxicillin may reduce methotrexate clearance and increase toxicity (mucositis, myelosuppression). Specialist review is required.
NSAIDs such as Ibuprofen can raise methotrexate levels and precipitate bone-marrow and kidney toxicity.
Ibuprofen plus Warfarin markedly increases gastrointestinal bleeding risk. Prefer an alternative analgesic.
Hold Metformin around iodinated contrast procedures in patients with reduced kidney function to lower lactic acidosis risk.
